prior_importants.description: `PERMALINK` takes the ref as a single segment (`[\w.-]+\/`). A link to a branch or tag whose name contains `/` (e.g. `feature/x`, `release/1.2`) is only partly stripped. Example: `https://github.com/acme/tool/blob/feature/x/src/claude/hooks.ts` becomes `x/src/claude/hooks.ts`. That path matches no ADR glob, and `moduleOf` returns undefined for it. So a bug whose Suspected area is that link gets `triggers: []` and `needsDesign: false`, while the bare `src/claude/hooks.ts` fires `adr-area`. This breaks the acceptance criterion "permalink matches same globs as bare path" for a realistic input, and the gate passes when it should fire. Before this PR the link didn't match either. The fault is in the new feature, not a regression.

findings.description: PERMALINK strips any `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob|tree/<ref>/` prefix whatever the owner and repo are, so a permalink to another project's source is now checked against this repo's modules and ADR globs. Before this change such a link stayed inert because its first segment is `github.com` and moduleOf returns undefined. Trigger: a bug ticket whose Suspected area reads `src/core/queue.service.ts; upstream cause at https://github.com/foo/lib/blob/main/src/runtime/pool.ts`. The second path becomes `src/runtime/pool.ts`, moduleOf counts `runtime` as a second module, and `module-boundary` fires, forcing a design for a one-module bug. Any ADR area such as `src/runtime/**` also fires `adr-area` on code that is not in this repo. It only ever over-fires, which the design leans toward, so this is a nit. Possible fix: strip only when owner/repo matches the project's remote, or drop paths from foreign-repo permalinks.
